name: AL-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+23 district lean makes this deeply Republican territory
Rogers holds a roughly 35-to-1 cash advantage over McInnis
Prediction markets price Rogers at 99% to win
No public polling or expert ratings; the challenger is underfunded and little known
model.rationale: The district's R+23 lean, Rogers' incumbency and roughly 35-to-1 fundraising advantage, and prediction markets pricing him at 99 percent leave McInnis without a visible path; even a strong Democratic midterm environment would still leave a wide Republican margin.
model.watch: Only a major scandal or an extraordinary anti-incumbent wave in this heavily Republican district would put the seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alabama's 3rd District sits firmly in Republican territory, with a partisan lean of roughly 23 points toward the GOP. Mike Rogers returns as the incumbent with a commanding financial position: he has raised $2.1 million and holds $2.6 million on hand. His Democratic challenger, Lee McInnis, has raised about $61,000 and reports under $10,000 in the bank.

No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters have flagged the race as competitive. Prediction markets give Rogers a 99 percent chance of winning. Even with a midterm environment that favors Democrats nationally, the district's heavy Republican lean and the money gap point to a Republican margin near twenty points. The realistic question is the size of Rogers' victory, not whether he wins.
